mainTopic: Which פסוקים are written on the סוטה's scroll, the drashos behind the dispute, and related אגדה about marriage and אברהם's rewards
overview: The משנה asks which פסוקים the כהן writes on the סוטה's scroll, which is later erased into her water. The first view, which the גמרא identifies as רבי מאיר, starts at 'ואם לא שכב איש' and skips the lines where the כהן makes her swear and where she answers 'אמן אמן'. רבי יוסי says nothing is skipped. רבי יהודה says only the two actual curse פסוקים are written. The גמרא shows that all three read one פסוק, 'וכתב את האלות האלה', word by word, each word either including or excluding. It defends רבי מאיר's reading: a ה follows the word it is attached to. רבי תנחום explains that the word 'הנקי' itself hints at a curse. The גמרא then turns to אגדה: רבי עקיבא on the שכינה between husband and wife, and רבא on the סוטה's dust and on the מצוות אברהם's children earned through his humility, תכלת and תפילין. A new משנה then begins listing materials the scroll may not be written on, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where does the priest start writing the scroll?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens by asking from which point in the פרשה of סוטה the כהן begins writing the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When the כהן comes to write the scroll, from what place in the Torah does he start writing?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its main question: which פסוקים go onto the סוטה's scroll. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll gets erased into the water the סוטה drinks, so its wording matters. The Torah's סוטה section is long, and the משנה wants to pin down exactly where the written portion begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. The opening of the משנה text.
The scroll on which the curse section is written and later erased into the water.
From what place. Here it means from which verse.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
When he comes to write the scroll,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן, and the scroll is the one for the סוטה.

phrases.english: from what place does he write?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting verse of the text written on the סוטה's scroll.

steps.title: He starts at the oath section
steps.stepSummary: The writing begins with 'ואם לא שכב איש' and continues into 'ואת כי שטית תחת אישך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He starts from 'And if no man has lain with you…' and continues with 'But if you have gone astray while under your husband…'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question. The writing starts where the כהן begins speaking the oath to the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוקים describe the procedure: bringing her, the מנחה, and so on. The scroll begins at the actual words of the oath, both the clearing line (if innocent) and the guilt line (if she strayed).

keyTerms.meaning: You went astray. You turned aside from your husband.
While under your husband. While married to him.
Etc. The rest of the verse is meant too.

phrases.english: From "And if no man has lain [with you], etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:19. The 'etc.' means the whole verse is written.

phrases.english: "But if you have gone astray while under your husband"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Writing starts at במדבר 5:19, the opening of the oath.

steps.title: What is skipped and what is written
steps.stepSummary: He skips the narrative line 'והשביע הכהן את האשה', writes the curse wording, and skips 'ואמרה האשה אמן אמן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not write 'Then the כהן shall make the woman swear'. He does write 'ה׳ shall make you a curse and an oath… and this cursing water shall enter your bowels, to make the belly swell and the thigh fall away'. He does not write 'And the woman shall say: אמן, אמן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists exactly which lines inside the section are left out and which are written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is clear. The words of the oath and curse go on the scroll. The narrative lines describing the כהן's action and the woman's reply do not. Those are instructions, not part of the curse itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall make [her] swear.
A curse.
An oath.
The water that brings the curse.

steps.confusionAlert: Skipping is not random. He skips only the 'stage directions' (the כהן makes her swear, she answers אמן) and keeps the curse words themselves.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא, only the oath and curse wording goes on the scroll. The descriptive lines around it are left out.

phrases.english: And he does not write
"Then the priest shall cause the woman to swear."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:21. This is the opening of that verse.

phrases.english: But he writes: "The Lord shall make you a curse and an oath."
"And this water that causes the curse shall go into your bowels"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:22

phrases.english: "to make the belly swell and the thigh fall away."
And he does not write
"And the woman shall say: Amen, amen."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינוֹ כּוֹתֵב וְהִשְׁבִּיעַ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הָאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer by detailing omissions within the section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative lines (the כהן administering the oath, the woman's אמן) are omitted. The curse wording is written.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: nothing is skipped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and holds that the כהן writes the section straight through without leaving anything out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: He would not interrupt. He writes everything in order.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion is brought. רבי יוסי rejects the skipping described in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא leaves out the narrative lines. רבי יוסי holds the scroll should contain the passage continuously, including those lines. The dispute is only about the omissions inside the section, not about where writing begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Interrupts. Here it means skipping parts of the text.

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת. The תנא קמא skips the narrative lines, while רבי יוסי writes the section without breaks.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
He would not interrupt.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן writes the lines straight through, without skipping the ones the first opinion left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר לֹא הָיָה מַפְסִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the omissions listed in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the passage is written continuously with no omissions.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only the actual curse verses are written
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that the כהן writes only the two curse פסוקים, from 'יתן ה׳ אותך לאלה' through 'ובאו המים המאררים', and leaves out 'ואמרה האשה אמן אמן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The כהן writes nothing except 'The Lord shall make you a curse and an oath...' and 'This cursing water shall enter your insides...'. He does not write 'And the woman shall say: Amen, amen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third opinion. רבי יהודה says the כהן writes the smallest amount: only the curse lines themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view in the משנה started earlier, at 'ואם לא שכב איש', and רבי יוסי said to write everything. רבי יהודה cuts it down to just the two curse פסוקים. Like the first view, he also leaves out the woman's 'אמן אמן'.

keyTerms.meaning: at all (literally: all of itself), used here to mean 'nothing at all except'
a curse
an oath
the water that brings the curse

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He does not write anything at all except
"The Lord shall make you a curse and an oath, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:21

phrases.aramaic: וּבָאוּ הַמַּיִם הַמְאָרְרִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּמֵעַיִךְ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "And this cursing water shall enter your insides, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:22

phrases.english: And he does not write "And the woman shall say: Amen, amen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, narrowest opinion after the first view and רבי יוסי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the two actual curse פסוקים are written; 'אמן אמן' is not written.

steps.title: What is the disagreement based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the source of the מחלוקת in the משנה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what the opinions in the משנה are really arguing about. This question sets up the next step, which names the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks for the root of the מחלוקת: which source makes each תנא decide how much to write. It does not argue against anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
about what do they disagree?

phrases.english: Gemara:
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's opinions to asking for their source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis of the מחלוקת about which parts of the section are written.

steps.title: They disagree about how to read one פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The מחלוקת depends on how to read 'וכתב את האלות האלה הכהן בספר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about this פסוק: 'And the כהן shall write these curses in a scroll.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole מחלוקת comes from one פסוק about the כהן writing the curses. The next steps show how each side reads its words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the כהן writes 'the curses'. The question is exactly which lines count as 'the curses'. Each small word in the פסוק (את, ה, אלה) becomes a clue.

keyTerms.meaning: a פסוק (verse)
curses
a scroll, here the מגילה of the סוטה

phrases.english: They disagree about this verse:
"And shall write these curses
the כהן in a scroll."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת depends on how to read 'וכתב את האלות האלה הכהן בספר'.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's word-by-word reading of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads each word as including or excluding. Actual curses and curses implied by blessings are written. The curses in דברים are not, and neither are the commands or the 'אמן' responses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: 'Curses' means actual curses. 'The curses' includes curses that come from the blessings. 'These' excludes the curses in משנה תורה. 'The these' excludes the commands and the 'amen' responses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי מאיר, the first opinion in the משנה, gets his view from the פסוק. He reads it one word at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אלות' alone means real curses. The extra 'ה' adds curses hidden inside blessings, like 'you will be clean' implying a curse if she is guilty. That is why he starts writing at 'ואם לא שכב איש'. 'אלה' limits the writing to this section and leaves out the curses of דברים. The extra 'ה' on 'האלה' removes the narrative commands and the 'אמן אמן'.

keyTerms.meaning: actual, real
to include (the word adds something)
to exclude (the word leaves something out)
ספר דברים
commands (like 'the כהן shall make her swear') and acceptances (her 'אמן')

steps.confusionAlert: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה is רבי מאיר. The גמרא names him here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
phrases.notes: He is the unnamed first opinion in the משנה.

phrases.english: "Curses" — actual curses.
"The curses" — to include
curses that come from the blessings.
phrases.notes: For example, 'be clean from this bitter water' hints at the opposite if she is guilty.

phrases.english: "These" — to exclude
the curses in Mishneh Torah.
"The these" — to exclude
the commands and the acceptances of "amen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the first opinion reads the פסוק given in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Actual curses and curses implied by blessings are written. Curses in דברים, commands and 'אמן' responses are not.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: 'את' brings back the commands and the 'אמן'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי accepts all of רבי מאיר's readings but says the word 'את' includes the commands and the acceptances, so everything is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי: All of it is as you said, but 'את' comes to include the commands and the acceptances.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי agrees with every reading רבי מאיר made. He adds one more word, 'את', which puts the commands and the 'אמן' back into the writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on what 'ה', 'אלה' and 'האלה' teach. The only difference is that רבי יוסי treats 'את' as a word that includes. It cancels the exclusion of the commands and acceptances, so he writes the section straight through.

keyTerms.meaning: as you said
a small word in the פסוק, read here as adding something

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת comes from one פסוק. רבי מאיר reads 'האלה' as excluding the commands and 'אמן'. רבי יוסי reads 'את' as bringing them back, so in his view everything is written.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei:
all of them are as you said,
"Et" — to include the commands and the acceptances.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבי מאיר's readings and adds 'את' to include what רבי מאיר left out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'את' includes the commands and the acceptances, so the whole section is written.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר does not agree with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר does not learn anything from the word 'את', so he does not include the commands and the acceptances.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? He does not learn anything from the word 'את'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי מאיר does not accept רבי יוסי's extra reading. As a rule, רבי מאיר does not learn from the word 'את'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי included the commands and the 'אמן' answers only because of the word 'את'. רבי מאיר does not learn from 'את' anywhere, so for him nothing is added. That is why he still leaves the commands and acceptances out.

keyTerms.meaning: The word 'את' each time it appears in the תורה
He does not learn a law from it
An inclusion, a word that adds more cases to the law

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking why רבי מאיר doesn't use the word 'את' the way רבי יוסי does in step 9.

phrases.english: He does not learn anything from the word 'את'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי מאיר does not accept the one extra reading that רבי יוסי added in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי מאיר does not include the commands and acceptances the way רבי יוסי does.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר never learns from the word 'את', so the word adds nothing for him.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads every word as leaving something out
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, 'אלות' means the actual curses. 'האלות' leaves out curses implied by blessings, 'אלה' leaves out the curses in משנה תורה, and 'האלה' leaves out the commands and acceptances.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה reads all the words as leaving things out. 'אלות' means the actual curses. 'האלות' leaves out curses that come from blessings. 'אלה' leaves out the curses in משנה תורה. 'האלה' leaves out the commands and the acceptances.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה reads the פסוק. For him, every word narrows the law, so only the actual curses are written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The big difference from רבי מאיר is the word 'האלות'. רבי מאיר used it to add the curses that are implied by the blessings, but רבי יהודה uses it to leave them out. That is why רבי יהודה writes only the two curse פסוקים, as we saw in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: As exclusions, words that leave cases out
The actual, openly stated curses
Curses that are only implied by the blessings
The book of דברים
The commands (such as 'השביע') and the acceptances ('אמן אמן')

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה both read 'אלה' and 'האלה' as leaving things out. They argue only about 'האלות': רבי מאיר says it includes curses implied by blessings, and רבי יהודה says it excludes them.

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה:
He reads all of them as exclusions.
'אלות' means actual curses.
'האלות' comes to exclude curses that come from blessings.
'אלה' comes to exclude the curses in משנה תורה.
'האלה' comes to exclude commands and acceptances.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה — כּוּלְּהוּ בְּמִיעוּטֵי דָּרֵישׁ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion's reading of the same פסוק, after רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every word in the פסוק narrows the law, so only the actual curses are written.

steps.title: Why does the letter ה include in one word and exclude in another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר can say the ה in 'האלות' includes while the ה in 'האלה' excludes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר, what is different about this ה, that it includes, and what is different about that ה, that it excludes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי מאיר's reading. He treats the same letter ה in two opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the ה of 'האלות' adds the curses implied by blessings. Yet the ה of 'האלה' leaves out the commands and acceptances. The same extra letter seems to be doing two opposite jobs, so the גמרא wants a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
The letter ה added at the start of a word
That it includes, adding more cases
That it excludes, leaving cases out

phrases.english: And according to רבי מאיר,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הַאי הֵי דִּמְרַבֵּי בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: what is different about this ה, that he includes with it,
phrases.notes: This is the ה of 'האלות'.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא הַאי הֵי דְּמַעֵיט בֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: and what is different about that ה, that he excludes with it?
phrases.notes: This is the ה of 'האלה'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, מַאי שְׁנָא הַאי הֵי דִּמְרַבֵּי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי מאיר's reading from step 8 and questions whether it is consistent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the same letter ה includes in 'האלות' but excludes in 'האלה' according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A ה follows the word it is attached to
steps.stepSummary: A ה next to an including word adds to the inclusion, and a ה next to an excluding word adds to the exclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ה next to an inclusion is an inclusion. A ה next to an exclusion is an exclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The ה does not have its own fixed meaning; it follows the word it is attached to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, 'אלות' is an including word, so its ה keeps including. 'אלה' is an excluding word, so its ה keeps excluding. This makes רבי מאיר's reading consistent after all.

keyTerms.meaning: That is next to
An inclusion
An exclusion

steps.whatToRemember: The extra ה takes on the job of its word. With 'אלות' it includes, and with 'אלה' it excludes.

phrases.english: A ה that is next to an inclusion is an inclusion,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Read it as 'הי דגבי ריבויא — ריבויא'.

phrases.english: and a ה that is next to an exclusion is an exclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ה follows the word it is attached to: next to an including word it includes, and next to an excluding word it excludes.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי מאיר does not infer a positive from a negative
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר can include curses implied by the blessings, since he does not hold that you can infer the opposite from a statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי מאיר does not hold that from a negative statement you can hear a positive one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי מאיר's view that the oath includes curses that come out of the blessings. He does not accept that kind of inference, so how can he learn curses from blessings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said the כהן's oath covers even curses hidden inside the blessings ('if you did not sin, be free' implies 'if you did sin, be harmed'). But that is exactly the logic of 'from a negative you hear a positive,' which רבי מאיר rejects elsewhere. So his reading seems to contradict his own principle.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
He does not hold of
From a negative statement you can infer the positive one

steps.confusionAlert: Steps 12-13 asked why the ה can include in one word and exclude in another. This challenge is different. It asks how 'curses that come from blessings', the very thing that ה of 'האלות' includes for רבי מאיר, can exist at all according to his own principle.

phrases.english: But רבי מאיר does not hold
that from a negative you can hear a positive?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִכְּלָל לָאו אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי מאיר's reading of the ה, the גמרא now challenges another part of his view: curses learned from blessings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's inclusion of curses implied by the blessings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Learning curses from blessings requires inferring a positive from a negative, a principle רבי מאיר rejects.

steps.title: רבי תנחום: the word הִנָּקִי hints at a curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום answers that the word 'הִנָּקִי' can be read as 'חִנָּקִי' (choke), so the blessing itself contains a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said: It is written 'הִנָּקִי.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי תנחום answers the challenge. The curse is not inferred by logic; it is hinted in the very word of the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הִנָּקִי' means 'be free,' but it sounds like 'חִנָּקִי,' 'choke.' Read together with the start of the next פסוק, 'if you went astray,' it becomes a direct curse. So רבי מאיר does not need the rule of inferring a positive from a negative.

keyTerms.meaning: Be free / cleared (the blessing word in the oath)
Choke (the curse hidden in the word)
It is written

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, the curse in the blessings comes from the wording 'הִנָּקִי' = 'חִנָּקִי,' not from inferring the opposite.

phrases.english: רבי תנחום said: 'You shall be free' is written.
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:19. He reads הִנָּקִי like חִנָּקִי, 'choke,' so the blessing word itself carries a curse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק so the curse is explicit in the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The curse in the blessings could only come by inferring a positive from a negative.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curse is built into the word הִנָּקִי, read as חִנָּקִי, so no such inference is needed.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the שכינה between husband and wife, or fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא teaches that if husband and wife are worthy, the שכינה is between them; if not, fire consumes them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא taught: A man and a woman, if they merit, the שכינה is between them. If they do not merit, fire consumes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי עקיבא, connected to the theme of faithfulness in marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אִישׁ and אִשָּׁה share the letters א and ש. אִישׁ adds a י and אִשָּׁה adds a ה, which together spell a name of ה'. Take away those letters, and both words become אֵשׁ, fire.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught / expounded
They merited
The Divine Presence
Fire consumes them

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא taught:
A man and a woman, if they merit, the Divine Presence is between them.
phrases.notes: The י of אִישׁ and the ה of אִשָּׁה together spell a name of ה'.

phrases.english: If they do not merit, fire consumes them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵישׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִישׁ וְאִשָּׁה זָכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the oath's wording to a new אגדה teaching about marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A faithful husband and wife have the שכינה between them; an unfaithful couple is consumed by fire.

steps.title: רבא: the woman's fire is stronger
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that the fire of the woman is stronger than that of the man, because in אִשָּׁה the letters א and ש are joined.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And the woman's fire is stronger than the man's. What is the reason? This one is joined, and that one is not joined.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds on רבי עקיבא's teaching and adds a difference between the man and the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אִשָּׁה, the א and ש stand right next to each other, forming אֵשׁ directly. In אִישׁ, the י separates them. So the woman's 'fire' is joined and stronger, while the man's is split.

keyTerms.meaning: Stronger / greater
What is the reason?
Joined together

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: אִישׁ + אִשָּׁה with י-ה = שכינה; without it = אֵשׁ. רבא: the woman's אֵשׁ is stronger because its letters are joined.

phrases.english: רבא said: And that of the woman is stronger than that of the man.
phrases.notes: He means the fire that consumes the woman.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
This one is joined, and that one is not joined.
phrases.notes: In אִשָּׁה the א and ש touch; in אִישׁ the י sits between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to רבי עקיבא's teaching in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The woman's fire is stronger, since the letters of אֵשׁ are joined in אִשָּׁה but separated in אִישׁ.

steps.title: Why the סוטה gets dust
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the dust in the סוטה's water points to two possible outcomes: a child like אברהם, or a return to dust in death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why did the תורה say to bring dust for the סוטה? If she is innocent, a son like אברהם אבינו will come from her, since אברהם called himself 'dust and ashes.' If she is guilty, she will go back to her dust.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new teaching about the dust put into the סוטה's water. The dust is a symbol that fits both possible outcomes of the test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dust has two meanings here. For an innocent woman it recalls אברהם, who called himself 'עפר ואפר,' so she will have a great son. For a guilty woman it recalls that people are made from dust and go back to it, meaning she will die.

keyTerms.meaning: Dust, which is placed into the סוטה's water
A wife suspected of being unfaithful, who is tested with the bitter water
She is worthy, meaning she is found innocent
She will go back to her dust, meaning she will die

steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the theme from רבי עקיבא and רבא in steps 16–17. The relationship between husband and wife can bring blessing or destruction.

phrases.english: Rava said:
For what reason did the Torah say
bring dust for the sotah?
If she is worthy, there will come out of her
a son like Abraham our forefather,
about whom it is written "dust and ashes",
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:27

phrases.english: if she is not worthy, she will return to her dust.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by רבא about the dust of the סוטה. It returns to the סוטה theme after the אגדה about husband and wife in steps 16–17, but does not build on the content of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dust in the סוטה's water hints at a son like אברהם if she is innocent, and at death if she is guilty.

steps.title: אברהם's humility earned two מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that because אברהם called himself 'dust and ashes,' his children were given two מצוות: the ashes of the פרה אדומה and the dust of the סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: As a reward for אברהם saying 'I am dust and ashes,' his children earned two מצוות: the ashes of the פרה and the dust of the סוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second teaching connected to the same words of אברהם. The 'ashes' match the פרה אדומה, and the 'dust' matches the סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word אברהם used is matched to a מצוה. 'אפר' (ashes) matches the ashes of the פרה אדומה, and 'עפר' (dust) matches the dust of the סוטה. His humility became a lasting gift for his children.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught publicly (a דרשה)
As a reward for
The ashes of the פרה אדומה, used to make people טהור
The dust put into the סוטה's water

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a count of exactly two מצוות. The next step will challenge that count.

phrases.english: Rava taught:
As a reward for what Abraham our forefather said,
"And I am dust and ashes",
his children merited two מצוות,
the ashes of the heifer and the dust of the sotah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרֵישׁ רָבָא: בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of אברהם's words 'עפר ואפר' from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם's humble words earned his children two מצוות: אפר פרה and עפר סוטה.

steps.title: What about the dust for covering blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's count of two: there is also a third מצוה with dust, כיסוי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the dust used for covering the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's list. If dust מצוות come from אברהם's reward, the dust of כיסוי הדם should be on the list too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said exactly two מצוות came from 'עפר ואפר.' But after slaughtering a wild animal or bird, you must cover its blood with dust. So why did רבא leave that one out?

keyTerms.meaning: But there is also (an opening for a challenge)
The מצוה of covering the blood of a slaughtered wild animal or bird with dust

phrases.english: But there is also
the dust for covering the blood!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's count of two מצוות in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that אברהם's children earned exactly two מצוות through his words.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כיסוי הדם is also a מצוה done with dust, so the list seems incomplete.

steps.title: Covering blood brings no benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dust of כיסוי הדם only completes a מצוה but gives no benefit, so it is not counted as a reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the dust helps complete a מצוה, but there is no benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why כיסוי הדם is left off the list. Only מצוות that bring real benefit count as אברהם's reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes of the פרה make a person טהור, and the dust of the סוטה can clear an innocent wife and bring peace at home. The dust of כיסוי הדם is a real מצוה, but it is done after the שחיטה and does not make anything permitted or bring any gain. A reward has to be something that benefits, so it is not counted.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that case
Completing or carrying out a מצוה
Benefit, real gain
There is not

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying כיסוי הדם is not a מצוה. It fully is. It only says no benefit comes from it, so it does not fit a list of 'rewards.'
steps.whatToRemember: אברהם's humility ('עפר ואפר') earned his children two beneficial מצוות: אפר פרה and עפר סוטה. כיסוי הדם is a מצוה with dust but gives no benefit, so it is not on the list.

phrases.english: There, there is completion of a מצוה,
but there is no benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a מצוה that only completes an act vs. a מצוה that brings real benefit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any מצוה done with dust should count as a reward from אברהם's words.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only מצוות that bring benefit (טהרה from the פרה, clearing the סוטה) count as reward. כיסוי הדם gives no benefit, so it is not counted.

steps.title: רבא: אברהם's thread and shoe strap earned two מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that because אברהם refused to take even 'a thread or a shoe strap,' his children merited תכלת and the strap of תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: As a reward for אברהם saying 'not a thread nor a shoe strap,' his children received two מצוות: the thread of תכלת and the strap of תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another 'reward' teaching, like his earlier one about dust and ashes. אברהם's refusal of a thread and a strap is repaid with a thread (תכלת) and a strap (תפילין).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same 'measure for measure' pattern as step 19. אברהם turned down a thread and a strap from the king of סדום, so his children were given a holy thread and a holy strap. The match is in the very same objects he refused.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded; taught a lesson from the פסוקים
As a reward for
The sky-blue thread in the ציצית
The leather strap of the תפילין
A shoe strap or shoelace

phrases.english: Rava expounded:
As a reward for what Avraham our father said:
"Not a thread nor a shoe strap,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:23. אברהם said this to the king of סדום, refusing to take anything of his.

phrases.english: his children merited two מצוות:
the thread of sky-blue wool
and the strap of tefillin.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא: בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new reward teaching by רבא, built the same way as his teaching in step 19 about dust and ashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם's refusal of a thread and a shoe strap earned his children the חוט של תכלת and the רצועה של תפילין.

steps.title: תפילין clearly bring honor, but what does תכלת bring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that תפילין are a fitting reward because they show God's name to the world, then asks what special benefit תכלת brings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The strap of תפילין makes sense, since the פסוק says the nations will see that God's name is called upon you, and רבי אליעזר הגדול says this means the head תפילין. But the thread of תכלת, what is special about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first explains why תפילין are a real reward, and then asks what makes תכלת a reward too. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like step 21, the גמרא assumes a reward must bring some real benefit or honor. תפילין clearly do: the head תפילין carry God's name and make the nations stand in awe. For תכלת no such benefit is obvious, so the גמרא asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense regarding... (opens a 'this part is fine, but...' question)
The תפילין worn on the head
What is it? What is its point?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting that תכלת is a מצוה. It is asking what honor or benefit it gives, since a reward should give something, just as step 21 said about dust.

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding the strap of tefillin,
as it is written:
"And all the peoples of the earth shall see
that the name of ה׳ is called upon you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 28:10

phrases.english: and it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
These are the tefillin of the head.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חוּט שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת, מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: But the thread of techeiles, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's statement by checking that each of the two מצוות is a real reward.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What benefit or honor does the חוט של תכלת give, that makes it a fitting reward?

steps.title: רבי מאיר: תכלת reminds us of the כסא הכבוד
steps.stepSummary: Through a ברייתא of רבי מאיר, the גמרא answers that תכלת looks like the sea, the sea like the sky, and the sky like the כסא הכבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי מאיר taught: Why was תכלת chosen over all other colors? Because תכלת looks like the sea, the sea looks like the sky, and the sky looks like the כסא הכבוד, as the פסוקים compare both the sky and the Throne to sapphire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. תכלת is special because its color is linked, step by step, to God's Throne of Glory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר builds a chain: תכלת is like the sea, the sea like the sky, the sky like the כסא הכבוד. Two פסוקים prove the last link: one compares the sky to sapphire, and the other compares the Throne to sapphire. So wearing תכלת ties a Jew to the Divine Throne, and that is the honor that makes it a fitting reward.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why is this one special?
Colors or dyes
The sky, the heavens
The Throne of Glory, God's Throne
Sapphire, a deep blue stone

steps.whatToRemember: אברהם refused a thread and a strap, so his children received the תכלת thread and the תפילין strap. Both bring real honor: תפילין show God's name to the nations, and תכלת recalls the כסא הכבוד through the chain sea → sky → Throne.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the גמרא insists that a 'reward' must bring a real benefit. It is the same point as step 21, where the dust of כיסוי הדם was not counted because it brings no benefit.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
What is different about techeiles
from all other kinds of colors?
Because techeiles is similar to the sea,
and the sea is similar to the sky,
and the sky is similar to the Throne of Glory —
as it says: "And they saw the God of Israel,
and under His feet was like a work of sapphire brick
and like the very heavens in clearness,"
phrases.notes: שמות 24:10. This פסוק shows that the sky looks like sapphire.

phrases.english: and it is written: "Like the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:26. The Throne also looks like sapphire, so the sky and the Throne look alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מָה נִשְׁתַּנָּה תְּכֵלֶת מִכׇּל מִינֵי צִבְעוֹנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by showing the special honor of תכלת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תכלת resembles the sea, which resembles the sky, which resembles the כסא הכבוד. So it links the wearer to God's Throne, and that is a real honor and a fitting reward.

steps.title: The משנה begins listing materials not allowed for the סוטה scroll
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. It rules that the כהן may not write the מגילת סוטה on a wooden tablet or on paper, and starts naming a third material that continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The כהן does not write the סוטה's scroll on a wooden tablet, and not on paper, and not on…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the stories about אברהם and brings a new משנה. This משנה starts a list of materials that are not allowed for writing the סוטה's scroll, and the list continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that the כהן writes the curses of the סוטה and erases them into the water. Now the משנה sets a rule about what he writes on: a wooden tablet and paper are ruled out. The words 'and not upon' show the list is not finished yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
The scroll with the curses that the כהן writes for the סוטה
A tablet, here one made of wood
Paper, here a kind made from grass or reeds

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off in the middle. 'And not upon' is not the end; the next section names the next material that is not allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
He does not write on a tablet,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן, and what he writes is the סוטה's scroll. The משנה just assumes you know this.

phrases.english: and not on paper, and not on…

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵינוֹ כּוֹתֵב לֹא עַל הַלּוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah about אברהם's rewards (Steps 22-24) and opens a new משנה about the halachos of writing the סוטה's scroll.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מגילת סוטה may not be written on a wooden tablet or on paper. More materials that are not allowed follow.
